title: Bangladesh’s first urban heatwave action plan, for Narayanganj
summary: Bangladesh’s first heat and health assessment, released in October 2026, reports that the country’s first urban heatwave action plan has been developed for Narayanganj, alongside national guidelines for heat-related illness and a public campaign, “Beat the Heat”.

review.note: Wording follows the report; dated to the assessment’s release because the plan’s own date is not given.

title: The first Global Heat Forum, in Bangkok
summary: Nearly 600 scientists, business leaders, philanthropists and health experts met in Bangkok from 6 to 9 October 2026. The Forum released the first country-level heat and health assessments for Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal, and a roadmap for investment and action on extreme heat.

review.note: Facts as stated by an organiser; no judgement of outcomes.

title: Support for the Southeast Asia Heat Health Hub’s next stage
summary: Announced on 8 October 2026: support for the next stage of the Global Heat Health Information Network’s Southeast Asia Hub, including funding for heat-health work in Indonesia (Makassar and two more cities) and Thailand in 2027, and preparations for a second Southeast Asia Heat Health Forum. The amount was not disclosed.
recipient: Global Heat Health Information Network, Southeast Asia Hub (NUS Medicine)

review.note: Role read as field-building: convening, shared evidence and country work; our reading, as on Follow the money.

title: A South Asia climate–health desk and a heat research consortium
summary: Announced on 20 February 2026: The Rockefeller Foundation and Wellcome fund a South Asia Climate–Health Desk under the WHO–WMO Climate and Health Joint Programme, and a South Asia Scientific Research Consortium, through a Rockefeller grant to IISER Pune, to develop tailored heat-risk thresholds. Amounts were not disclosed.
recipient: WHO–WMO South Asia Climate–Health Desk; IISER Pune research consortium

review.note: Role read as evidence: thresholds, research and decision tools; our reading.

title: How do heat-health pilots keep their footing once funding ends?
summary: A funder’s own account of the region notes that successful pilots often lose their institutional footing once funding ends.
question: How do heat-health pilots in Southeast Asia keep their institutional footing once their first funding ends?
why_it_matters: Protection that stops when a grant stops leaves people where they started; knowing what keeps it going would shape how grants are designed.
would_answer_it: Follow a handful of heat-health pilots for two years after their first funding, recording who kept which part going and why.
scale: Five to eight pilots, two years

review.note: Drawn from the funder’s stated observation; the question and approach are our suggestion.

title: Four South Asian countries formalise a heat cooperation framework
summary: A secondary web report says India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan formalised a regional coalition on heat in October 2026.

review.note: Established sources describe four country assessments released at the Global Heat Forum, not a formal coalition. Held until an official source confirms one.
